correctness.rationale: The proof works for arbitrary admissible operators, not only scalar tapers. Independently, write D_n=R_{nn} in level blocks, and x_n=Tr(D_n)/r. The (n+1,n) block of the commutator is D_n-D_{n+1}; retaining only these blocks and using the trace Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives the lower bound r times the scalar Dirichlet energy of x. The scalar problem allows summable infinite tails, but the displayed optimizer is finite. For b=B/r>1, (m+1)/3<b≤(m+2)/3 gives q>0 and −q<p≤q, so all positive cells decrease to zero and the finite sums give x_0=1 and trace B. The discrete Laplacian is −2q on cells 1 through m−1 and −(p+q) at m; expanding about the candidate yields exactly the nonnegative budget, boundary, tail and square terms in the proof. Equality is unique; equality at an operator midpoint would force the difference to commute with the shift, and a compact such difference is zero since T^n is weakly null and isometric. Trace r forces R=P directly and its commutator has squared norm r. At b=(m+2)/3 the parameters (p,q)=(q,q) switch to (−q,q) on the next support, with q=1/[m(m+1)], leaving the profile and first derivative unchanged. The second derivatives jump and m=3b+O(1) gives the leading 4r²/(9B) and the claimed 8/9 ratio. The bundled rational checks are supplemental; the script was read, not executed.
